literature: Lunar traverse planning guideline (traverses on slopes < 20 deg), Pena-Asensio et al. 2023, Acta Astronautica, doi:10.1016/j.actaastro.2023.10.010, as quoted in Universe Today / phys.org (Oct 2023)
ASSUMPTION: start of the 'slow, careful' band below the 20 deg hard limit
ASSUMPTION: ~0.5 m of local relief within 8 m is treated as a blocky field a suited crew should avoid
Apollo 15 crew average walking speed rose from ~1 km/h (EVA 1) to ~2 km/h (EVA 2), Apollo Lunar Surface Journal, NASA (https://www.nasa.gov/wp-content/uploads/static/history/alsj/a11/a11.gaits.html)
Apollo planners assumed 2.7 km/h for walkbacks longer than an hour (3.6 km/h for one hour), Apollo Lunar Surface Journal, NASA
Shape of Tobler's hiking function (Tobler 1993, NCGIA Technical Report 93-1), normalized to v_flat; ASSUMPTION that the Earth hiking shape applies to suited walking on Mars
ASSUMPTION: large bedforms (ripple ridges, soft crests) slow walking ~40%
xEMU designed for EVAs up to 8 h (6 +/- 2 h), NASA Lunar Surface EVA Concept of Operations (2020), https://www.nasa.gov/wp-content/uploads/2020/01/topic_1-_eva_lunar_surface_concept_of_operations.pdf
Legacy EMU: 8 h primary life support + 30 min backup life support (NASA EMU documentation; summarized on Wikipedia 'Extravehicular Mobility Unit')
Apollo planners treated a ~5 h time-in-suit limit as the main constraint on rover-assisted traverses, NTRS 19700009560 (https://ntrs.nasa.gov/api/citations/19700009560/downloads/19700009560.pdf)
~10 km max excursion a suited crew could walk back from after a rover failure (https://core.ac.uk/works/15254764)
ASSUMPTION: observe, photograph, and sample one outcrop
ASSUMPTION: ~4 min per tube for 10 tubes, loaded onto the rover
Wilson et al. 2008 / Sanchez-Lavega et al. 2023, JGR Planets, doi:10.1029/2022JE007480 (dust from pressure tide)
Hassler et al. 2014, Science 343, doi:10.1126/science.1244797 (RAD surface dose reference)
ai_use: Pipeline code written with AI assistance (Claude); all data values come from the listed NASA and USGS sources, and every processing step is in pipeline/.
